PASS for the distinct restricted A–E audit. The entire supplied manuscript and all five ordinary notes support the stated explicit family. Original S09 completion remains false: neither the unrestricted implication nor a counterexample with unequal obstacle envelopes is supplied. The historical first INCONCLUSIVE and cold candidate=false therefore remain correctly scoped.

A, including n2. The radial Hessian calculation is correct: qσ′>0 and qσ″>0 give tangential and radial eigenvalues qσ′/R² and qσ″/R². Each cutoff transition has a finite negative Hessian bound relative to positive h. The common choice δj=min(2^(−j),ej/(1+Kj,β+Kj,β′)) handles both exponents; subsequent arguments work for every allowed positive coefficient choice. The author’s flattening satisfies qA″=qσ″ζ+(qσ′/A)ζ′≥0. Increasing A increases qA′ and decreases qA; the fixed transition eventually remains unchanged. The centre values tend to −∞, and radial integrability supplies L¹ convergence. The cold route independently establishes the logarithmic pole, then composes its finite truncations with the convex increasing profile. Those truncations respect the stated logarithmic domain s≤0.

Uniform atlas-volume bounds and rescaling give summable termwise L¹ norms, regardless of overlap. The actual nonpositive partial sums decrease and converge in L¹ to limits finite almost everywhere. One fixed quadratic on each smaller chart corrects the entire sequence into psh functions. Thus its actual pointwise limits are proper canonical quasi-psh functions, rather than null-set replacements. Distributional passage retains h+Du,h+Dw≥(1−Σej)h≥3h/4. Each prescribed centre is an actual pole because its own negative term is already −∞ there. Density consequently excludes local boundedness on every nonempty open set. Additional poles are permitted. Finite prescribed sets require only stopping the sums.

B, including n2 and author applications 3 and 9. For Mt=supL≥1(Lβ−tLβ′), the boundary value is 1−t when t≥β/β′; otherwise the maximum is (1−β/β′)(β/(tβ′))^(β/(β′−β)). Both branches are finite and agree at the threshold. With S=Σδj≤1, termwise cutoff multiplication gives tw≤u+MtS, hence the cold bound tw≤u+Mt. The author’s constant satisfies tMauthor_(1/t)=Mt. These inequalities pass to actual canonical sums. In particular w≤u, so every pole of u is a pole of w; common infinities are never subtracted. The SAME w works for every real 0<t≤1. Convexity with zero makes tw genuine h-psh. The author’s shift w−Mauthor_bS and the cold shift w−bM_(1/b) each establish the original every-b stretching inequality. Together with u≤0, this proves u∈E_env(X,h,0).

C, including n3 and author applications 4–5. Both countable Jensen arguments are valid. The author uses weights δj/S and a neutral tail; the cold proof uses λj=2^(−j), δj/λj≤1, and the same neutral-tail device. For each fixed real s>0, uniform polar estimates control the single-profile exponentials. The radial exponent −ny+sS(1+y)^σ is integrable for both σ<1. The cold explicit constant Cs=n/2+(1−p)s(2sp/n)^(p/(1−p)), p=β′, also correctly bounds s(1+y)^p−ny/2. Integrating Jensen gives bounds independent of the number of terms. Monotone convergence then proves exponential integrability for the ACTUAL countable limits at every real positive scale. Holomorphic germs are bounded on smaller neighborhoods, and smooth positive dV is locally comparable with Lebesgue measure. Hence I(su)=O_X, and the cold additional assertion I(sw)=O_X is also valid. No valuation, Lelong-number, or finite-sum shortcut is used.

The [Demailly 2012 manuscript](https://www.ime.usp.br/~cordaro/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Jean-Pierre-Demailly-Complex-Analytic-and-Differential-Geometry-1.pdf), pp.34–40, matches premises 0–5; their relevant statements and provided proof contexts were checked. Premise 0 applies separately to the smooth pole flattenings and countable partial sums, with fixed quadratic corrections and independently established properness. Premise 1 identifies canonical finite maxima after a common correction. Premises 2–3 apply to both complete competitor families, which are locally uniformly bounded above and have genuine anchors. Premise 4 supplies canonical current equivalence and final uniqueness. Premise 5 has the necessary radial-kernel and properness qualifications. The positive normalization factor in D changes none of these positivity statements.

The author’s finite-max/Choquet route is valid independently of the cold route. Convolution gives Dvi,ε≥−h−ηεD|z|² with ηε→0. The smooth maximum has nonnegative first derivatives summing to one and positive semidefinite second derivative, so it preserves that lower bound. Its L¹ limit gives the EXACT bound for the canonical finite maximum. Choquet selection on a finite chart cover yields a countable subfamily with the same regularized supremum. Including a genuine anchor in every finite maximum provides integrable domination between that anchor and F. The maxima converge in L¹ to the regularized supremum, and their exact current inequality passes distributionally. The quadratic correction alone is never mistaken for the exact h inequality.

The cold n1 constant-form/reverse-Fatou route is also valid. Its disk Green formula has the correct factor 1/(2π). Line submeans, directional averaging and upper semicontinuity recover canonical ball-average values, including −∞. Convolution and reverse Fatou establish the current-to-psh implication for already genuine quasi-psh representatives. Decreasing limits use a fixed correction and the separately proved L¹ bound. For upper envelopes, translated disk inequalities and a common finite upper bound justify reverse Fatou; the lower member ensures properness and local integrability. To recover the exact variable-background bound, Hx=θ(x)+εω satisfies θ≤Hx≤θ+2εω on suitable neighborhoods. Testing the resulting inequalities against positive test forms, localized by a nonnegative partition of unity, and letting ε→0 removes the error. No derivatives of that partition are taken. This proves the claimed exact inequality even for nonclosed θ, without assuming a local curvature potential.

D, including n4 and author applications 6–8. For every continuous F, the unrestricted family has the constant min F as an anchor. Both envelope routes therefore give a genuine bounded W=P_h(F), with min F≤W≤F≤max F canonically. Since I(su)=O_X for every real s, EVERY genuine h-psh v satisfies the original ideal-INCLUSION order; the entire ideal competitor family is exactly the unrestricted family.

The author’s At=(1−t)W+tw−t‖F‖∞ is genuine, below F, and ordinarily dominated by u with a finite t-dependent constant. Independently, the cold Vt=(1−t)W+t(w−K), K=max(0,−min F), is below W and has the same ordinary-order property. These establish nonempty ordinary competitor families and proper L¹ anchors before applying the envelope lemmas. Thus At≤O≤W, or Vt≤O≤W, for O=P_{h,F}[u]. Their limits recover W wherever w is finite, giving O=W almost everywhere. A common quadratic correction and canonical uniqueness, independently reconstructed through ball averages in n1, give equality at EVERY point. The raw ordinary supremum can remain −∞ at poles; its upper regularization is essential. For F=0, the unrestricted envelope and both singularity envelopes are exactly the genuine function zero.

All eight support edges were checked: n2→n1; n3→n2; n4→n1,n2,n3; n5→n2,n3,n4. Each cited result supplies its required hypotheses, and the graph is acyclic. For n5, the displayed grid has 1009 values, giving 9081 and 24216 comparisons. Its scalar specializations and geometric-sum identities follow from the independently checked formulas. These remain finite diagnostics. Reported execution, environment, hashes and process receipts are provenance; their execution is not certified, and no protected histories, stdout, output.json or artifact trees were inspected.

E is truthful. Positivity of h and the explicitly constructed stronger w are restrictions of this family. No BMP, positive lower type volume, exceptional mass geometry, top-product mass, unbounded-product passage or literature priority is established. Applicability to a GIVEN positive h with an exceptional mass property is conditional and requires no existence claim about such a geometry. The original definitions and completion criterion remain intact; the unrestricted original question is unresolved by this work.

Harmless wording clarification: the old phrase “constant near0” refers to the spatial centre. The logarithmic profile is constant for s≤−2A, exactly as the manuscript already states. No substantial mathematical repair is required. No indispensable unresolved application remains within the restricted A–E scope.

passages.statement: On open Ω⊂ℂⁿ, decreasing plurisubharmonic sequences have plurisubharmonic pointwise limits, allowing identically −∞ components (Demailly I.5.4).
On open Ω⊂ℂⁿ, finite pointwise maxima of plurisubharmonic functions are plurisubharmonic, including common −∞ values (Demailly I.5.6).
A nonempty locally uniformly bounded-above plurisubharmonic family on open Ω⊂ℂⁿ has a plurisubharmonic regularized supremum equal almost everywhere to its raw supremum (Demailly I.5.7).
A nonempty locally uniformly bounded-above upper semicontinuous family Ω→[−∞,+∞), Ω⊂ℝᵐ open, has a countable subfamily with the same regularized supremum (Demailly I.4.23).

On open Ω⊂ℂⁿ, locally integrable plurisubharmonic functions have positive distributional complex Hessians; real distributions whose Hessians are positive in every constant complex direction have unique locally integrable plurisubharmonic representatives (Demailly I.5.8).

For open Ω⊂ℂⁿ and plurisubharmonic u not identically −∞ on any component, convolutions with ρ_ε(z)=ε^(−2n)ρ(z/ε), where ρ is nonnegative smooth radial, unit-integral and supported in B(0,1), are smooth plurisubharmonic on {dist(z,ℂⁿ\Ω)>ε} and decrease pointwise to u as ε↓0 (Demailly I.5.5).
